> `cwcli apps install` can now be asked to *ensure* an app is installed rather than to install it fresh, and it no longer fails on a bench that already carries the app.

### New Features

* `cwcli apps install --if-not-present` (also `cwcli axi apps install --if-not-present`) turns install into an idempotent "ensure installed" operation: an app already installed on a target site is reported as a skipped step and the command exits 0 without re-running its install hooks, while an app the site lacks still installs normally and a genuine failure still exits non-zero.
This is opt-in: upgrading changes nothing on its own, and without the flag an already-installed app is still refused.
It is not a `--force`: there is still no way to reinstall over an app the site already has.

### Bug Fixes

* `cwcli apps install` no longer fails when the app directory already exists under the bench's `apps/` (as on a pre-warmed base image).
It skips the fetch and proceeds to install on the site instead of failing the whole command at the fetch step.
* The `axi` Docker-unreachable error previously had no guidance.
It now carries a next-step hint pointing at the same fix `cwcli doctor` gives.
